sentences.text: Brachyspira is a genus of anaerobic spirochetes that includes nine officially recognised species, several of which are pathogenic to mammals and birds.
In humans the bacteria attach intimately to the colonic mucosa, and a decade-long pathology study diagnosed intestinal spirochetosis from a basophilic band on the colonic epithelial surface.
That study reports intestinal spirochetosis in about 1% of human colonic biopsy specimens and attributes it to Brachyspira pilosicoli and Brachyspira aalborgi.
A profile article describes Brachyspira colonisation of humans as common in populations from developing countries and in HIV-positive patients, and rarely investigated as a human pathogen.
A pooled analysis of 113 patients reported that those infected with Brachyspira pilosicoli more often had diarrhea, fever, HIV and immunocompromised conditions.
